papers.title_in_file: Neural-network-assisted Monte Carlo sampling trained by Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results (spectral gap and magnetization), conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study of a hybrid MCMC method in which a neural sampler trained on QAOA samples proposes moves for Boltzmann sampling of spin glasses.

assertions.value: The authors report that the method improves the spectral gap by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to the uniform distribution, particularly at low temperatures.
quotes: The proposed method improves the spectral gap by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to the uniform distribution, particularly at low temperatures
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from numerical experiments in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The gain is measured against a uniform proposal and other classical proposals in simulation, not on quantum hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that the spectral gap experiment covers 100 randomly generated instances for each system size, from 3 to 12 spins.
assertions.anchor: Section IV A, Spectral gap analysis, p.5
quotes: In this experiment, we compute the spectral gap for 100 randomly generated instances for each system size n, ranging from 3 to 12 spins
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section IV A.

assertions.value: The authors state that at high temperatures classical proposals are sufficiently efficient and outperform the proposed method, and that the method is not intended for high-temperature settings.
assertions.anchor: Appendix, spectral gap versus temperature (Fig. 8 discussion)
quotes: classical proposals are sufficiently efficient and outperform the proposed method.
Therefore, it is not intended for high-temperature settings.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope limit in the Fig. 8 discussion.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is an open question whether the numerical advantage extends to larger models, and that noise in quantum devices could reduce the benefit.
assertions.anchor: Section V, Conclusion and outlook, p.9
quotes: An important open question is whether this numerical advantage extends to larger models.
noise in quantum devices could potentially reduce the numerical benefits of the proposed method.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit in Section V, p.9.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning and Grover's Algorithm for Quantum Optimization of Robotic Manipulators
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, methods/implementation, results (timing section) and conclusion; not the full derivation sections.
papers.what_it_is: A framework that trains a parameterized quantum circuit to model robot forward kinematics and uses it as a Grover oracle for kinematic optimization.

assertions.value: The authors report speedups of up to 93x over classical optimizers like Nelder-Mead as problem dimensionality increases.
quotes: up to 93x over classical optimizers like
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical timing result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The 93x figure is a wall-clock comparison of the quantum pipeline against classical optimizers on one problem, not a complexity result.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the 1-DoF case the quantum approach required 2.0 seconds against 1.1 seconds for Nelder-Mead (0.55x speedup), and attribute this to quantum overhead on simple problems.
quotes: For the 1-DoF case, the quantum approach required 2.0 seconds compared to 1.1 seconds for Nelder-Mead (0.55x speedup), indicating quantum overhead dominates for simple problems
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The abstract describes the demonstrations as simulated 1-DoF, 2DoF and dual-arm tasks, while the methods section states the circuits were executed on IBM's ibm_brisbane processor after validation on a simulator.
quotes: Demonstrated on simulated 1-DoF, 2DoF, and dual-arm manipulator tasks
executed on IBM's ibm_brisbane superconducting quantum processor
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statements of its setup, abstract and implementation section.
assertions.reader_inference: The two statements differ on whether the runs were simulated or on hardware. The coordinator should decide which one to cite for the speedup.

papers.title_in_file: Application of time-series quantum generative model to financial data
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, numerical experiments, results, conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A numerical test of a time-series quantum generative model on GOOGLE and IBM stock data, compared with LSTM and VAR.

assertions.value: The authors state that the time-series quantum generative model yielded the same accuracy as LSTM with fewer parameters.
quotes: Consequently, we confirmed that the time-series quantum generative model yielded the same accuracy as LSTM with fewer parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on two stocks.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is with LSTM only. VAR was the best method in most cases (next assertion).

assertions.value: The authors report that in most cases the VAR model gave the best prediction accuracy.
quotes: In many cases, VAR provided the best outcome.

assertions.reader_inference: The quantum model did not beat the best classical baseline in this study.

papers.partial_detail: Annotation, introduction, contents, Lecture 4 (Grover search) and Section 4.2 (limits of quantum speedup). Other lectures only skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A university lecture course on quantum computing, including Grover search and the limits of quantum speedup.

assertions.value: The author states that the course is designed for students of physics and mathematics and natural science specialties as well as all those interested in the subject.
quotes: The course is designed for students of physics and mathematics and natural science specialties as well as all those interested in this subject.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own audience and scope, Annotation.

assertions.value: The author states, citing earlier work, that Grover's algorithm is optimal in an exact sense: any algorithm that works significantly faster gives an incorrect answer for the iterative task for the vast majority of functions.
quotes: It can be shown (see [13]) that this algorithm is optimal in the following exact sense.
Any other algorithm that works significantly faster will give an incorrect answer for the iterative task (35) for the vast majority of functions
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the lectures attribute to cited work, not proved in the text.

assertions.value: The author states that it is impossible to obtain more than a quadratic quantum speedup for most classical algorithms, and that quantum speedup of classical calculations is a rare phenomenon.
assertions.anchor: Section 4.2, Quantum speedup of classical computations and its limits
quotes: it is impossible to obtain more than a quadratic quantum spedup for most classical algorithms.
Thus, the quantum spedup of classical calculations is a rare phenomenon.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the lectures take from the author's earlier work and cited theorem, not re-proved here.
assertions.reader_inference: The statement is about black-box iteration of classical functions, not about all computational problems.

papers.title_in_file: Global optimization in variational quantum algorithms via dynamic tunneling method
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, simulation results, conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A global optimizer for variational quantum algorithms that adapts dynamic tunneling to a distance measure on quantum states, tested on VQE for the transverse-field Ising model.

assertions.value: The authors report that their simulation results demonstrate enhanced performance of the modified dynamic tunneling method over the conventional one as a global optimization algorithm.
quotes: Our simulation results demonstrate the enhanced performance of the modified dynamic tunneling method as a global optimization algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is against the conventional dynamic tunneling method and plain gradient descent, not against other global optimizers.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithm is applied to the variational quantum eigensolver for the transverse-field Ising model.
quotes: Our global optimization algorithm is applied to the variational quantum eigensolver for the transverse-field Ising model
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own test scope, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that the success of the algorithm is sensitive to the choice of the hyperparameters, and that a practical distance measure needs further investigation.
quotes: the success of the algorithm is also sensitive to an appropriate choice of the value of the hyperparameters.
a further investigation of the distance measure concerning a practical implementation of the flow is required
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limits in Section 4.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Measurement for Quantum Chemistry on a Quantum Computer
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusions. Technical sections skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A review of measurement techniques for quantum chemistry on quantum computers, mainly for VQE and QPE.

assertions.value: The authors state that the review emphasizes foundational concepts and methodologies rather than numerical benchmarks.
quotes: This review emphasizes foundational concepts and methodologies rather than numerical benchmarks
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that current hardware constraints restrict practical applications predominantly to small molecular systems.
quotes: Nonetheless, current hardware constraints restrict practical applications predominantly to small molecular systems
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement about the state of the field, with no single study behind it.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Hadamard test suffers from large measurement and quantum circuit costs to implement in practice.
quotes: it suffers from large measurement and quantum circuit costs to implement in practice.

papers.title_in_file: Machine Learning Approach towards Quantum Error Mitigation for Accurate Molecular Energetics
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, theory, results and conclusions.
papers.what_it_is: A graph neural network and regression model (GraphNetMitigator) that learns noise from shallow sub-circuits to mitigate VQE energies for small molecules, tested under simulated noise.

assertions.value: The authors report orders of magnitude improvements in predicted energy over a few strongly correlated molecules.
quotes: We demonstrate orders of magnitude improvements in predicted energy over a few strongly correlated molecules.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on a few molecules.
assertions.reader_inference: The study tests two molecules (H4 and BH) on simulated noise profiles, so the scope is small.

assertions.value: The authors state that they test the model on two different molecules and two different devices with diverse noise profiles, and that the simulation uses a fixed seed to represent averaged sampling statistics throughout.
quotes: we test it on two different molecules and two different devices with diverse noise profiles.
In a simulation protocol, this can be approximated by using a fixed seed value to represent an averaged sampling statistics which we have chosen to use throughout this work.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section III.
assertions.reader_inference: The results are simulated with device noise profiles, not measured on live hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that generalizing the model across diverse and larger classes of Hamiltonians and ansatze is an important future research direction.
assertions.anchor: Section IV, Conclusions and future outlook
quotes: One important future research direction is the generalization of the model across diverse and larger classes of Hamiltonians and ansatze.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit in Section IV.
